answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a small refundable stake before it may transact, like a quill signing a bond in ink that cannot be forged twice. Reputation then grows only through attested useful work, and a juniper-like slow-growing trust graph makes mass fake identities expensive: creating a thousand sock puppets means locking a thousand stakes. On the horizon, peers slash the stake of any agent caught duplicating work, so attacking costs more than it earns.
